statement: The Serbian Nemanjić dynasty and the Bulgarian tsardom competed for Balkan hegemony and Byzantine succession throughout the 13th–14th centuries. Stefan Nemanja allied with the Bulgarians against Byzantium; his successors alternately competed and cooperated with Bulgaria. Stefan Dušan's conquest of much of Bulgaria's western Macedonian territories (1330s) as part of his Balkan empire-building directly weakened Bulgaria before the Ottoman advance. The Bulgarian-Serbian competition prevented Balkan Christian unity and created the fragmented political landscape that the Ottomans exploited.
